title: New Indole-Bearing N-Acylhydrazone Derivatives: In Vitro Antibacterial, Anti-Inflammatory and Antioxidant Evaluation
content: Background/Objectives: Bacterial infections remain a major clinical challenge, particularly when biofilm formation reduces antimicrobial susceptibility and contributes to persistent infections. Inflammation and oxidative stress are also associated with infection progression and tissue damage, highlighting the potential value of compounds with antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant activities. This study aimed to evaluate the biological activities of five indole-bearing N-Acylhydrazone (NAH) derivatives with different phenyl-ring substituents. Methods: Antibacterial and antibiofilm activities were evaluated against selected Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. Cytotoxicity and nitric oxide (NO) inhibition were assessed in RAW 264.7 macrophages, while antioxidant activity was evaluated using DPPH and ABTS radical-scavenging assays. Results: Compound 3, bearing a 3,4-dichloro substituent, exhibited the strongest antibacterial activity against the tested Gram-positive bacteria, with minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values ranging from 3.91 to 15.63 µg/mL. It also showed 90% biofilm inhibition at 3.91 µg/mL against Staphylococcus aureus and Bacillus cereus. Compound 5, bearing a 4-fluoro substituent, demonstrated 95.85 ± 3.13% NO inhibition at 15 µg/mL while maintaining cell viability above 70%. In the DPPH assay, compound 2, bearing a 2,4-dichloro substituent, exhibited the highest radical-scavenging activity among the derivatives (84.19 ± 1.73% at 1 mg/mL). Conclusions: The findings suggest that the type and position of phenyl-ring substituents influence the biological activities of indole-bearing NAH derivatives. Further mechanistic studies, molecular docking, and structural optimization are required to identify potential biological targets and improve the activity and selectivity of these derivatives.
